verify.deploymentCorrectOracle: The RECURRENT no-spec DECODE is deployment-correct for token-by-token generation; the chunked re-prefill is a stricter-than-reality proxy — BUT with an important asymmetry (see notes). Code evidence: when vLLM serves WITHOUT speculation, every generated token is a single-token step (query_len==1) -> split_decodes_and_prefills returns it as a DECODE (utils.py L489-... decode_threshold=1) -> gdn_linear_attn.py L1163 elif num_decodes>0 -> fused_recurrent / fused_sigmoid_gating recurrent roll (and _forward_core_decode_non_spec L1261-1307 uses causal_conv1d_update + fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode = single-step recurrent). The model's served GDN state at decode is therefore built by the RECURRENT single-step roll, never re-chunked. The teacher-force oracle, by re-prefilling prompt+served[:i] as a fresh multi-token prefill, routes that same state through chunk_gated_delta_rule — a DIFFERENT kernel/reduction-order than what deployment uses. So the lossless reference that matches no-spec deployment = recurrent no-spec decode. CONFIRMED: the chunked re-prefill is NOT what deployment does at decode; it is a proxy that adds a chunk-vs-recurrent realization gap on top of any real defect. CAVEAT (deployment-faithful nuance): the LIVE TREE arm builds spine state via the SPEC recurrent kernel (fused_sigmoid_gating, IS_SPEC_DECODING) which is yet a THIRD realization — not byte-identical to the no-spec packed-decode recurrent kernel either; both are recurrent rolls (same algebra, ~1 ULP apart) and both differ from chunked. The directive's own anchor "oracle=no-spec NOT prefill" is therefore VIOLATED by the current instrument: it implements the no-spec oracle via per-position chunked PREFILL, exactly the path the directive names.
verify.offByOneRelation: The directive's two notes are causally linked: the streamed top_logprobs OFF-BY-ONE is WHY the instrument chose chunked per-position re-prefill. Per FR13_GOLD_MARGIN_BIND.md L29-37, the TREE arm's LIVE-STREAMED top_logprobs array is misaligned at spec-decode accept positions (~12/128 positions: served-token != reported-argmax) — a vLLM logprob-REPORTING quirk on the recurrent spec-decode serve stream. Trusting the recurrent stream's own logprobs is unreliable, so the author switched to CLEAN max_tokens=1 teacher-forced distributions on the byte-identical prefix (L35-36). That fix is correct for getting a clean per-position distribution, but it has the side effect of rebuilding GDN state via the CHUNKED prefill scan (query_len>1) instead of the recurrent roll — trading an off-by-one alignment problem for a chunk-vs-recurrent frame mismatch. A CORRECT recurrent capture CAN avoid both: feed served tokens one-at-a-time as single-token decodes (query_len==1 -> recurrent path) with persisted recurrent state and read each step's distribution directly (no streamed-array indexing, so no off-by-one), OR correct the off-by-one alignment of a single streaming no-spec decode. So the off-by-one is an alignment bug in the STREAM-READING, not an intrinsic blocker to a recurrent oracle; the instrument over-corrected from "unreliable recurrent stream logprobs" all the way to "chunked re-prefill," changing the kernel frame in the process.
verify.recommendedInstrument: Cleanest = OPTION (b): a sequential single-token no-spec DECODE oracle. Drive the server with fr10_decode_mode forcing the NON-spec (regular decode) path and feed served tokens one at a time so each step has query_len==1 -> num_decodes>0 -> recurrent roll (gdn_linear_attn.py L1163 / _forward_core_decode_non_spec). Read each step's max_tokens=1 distribution directly per step (not from a streamed array) -> no off-by-one. This reproduces exactly the no-spec deployment kernel and gives a per-position argmax+top-k for the full-stream flip re-score. BLOCKER / cost: vLLM continuous-batching does not natively expose "advance one token and return the decode-step distribution with persisted recurrent state" via /v1/completions — a single /v1/completions for prompt+served[:i] re-prefills (chunked) rather than decoding from a persisted recurrent state, because (i) Qwen3-Next lacks supports_mamba_prefix_caching so cross-request recurrent state is not preserved at sub-block granularity, and (ii) the API has no "resume from saved SSM state" hook. So a true recurrent re-score needs an in-process harness (load the model, run a genuine single-step decode loop over served_ids carrying ssm_state/conv_state forward) OR the q1 per-path recurrent oracle (OPTION c) generalized to every position — q1 already built this for ONE row (boot4 row6 pos849) via fr13_prefill_gdn_state_replay-style capture; scaling it to every served position is the straightforward (if GPU-heavy) path and needs NO API change. OPTION (a) single streaming no-spec decode with corrected off-by-one is cheapest IF the off-by-one alignment in the stream reader can be pinned, but the streamed-logprob quirk is in vLLM's reporting and was explicitly distrusted, so (b)/(c) in-process recurrent loop is the robust recommendation. NOTE this is Verify-phase: recommend, do not build — and the q1 deep-row result (recurrent oracle argmax=3425 vs tree=1970, flip PERSISTS) means the re-score is genuinely needed to settle whether the frontier shrinks, not assumed.
verify.notes: CRITICAL caveat for the Adversarial/reward-hack phase (do NOT let the frame story over-claim): q1_summary.json shows that vs the TRUE recurrent oracle the L0 first-nonzero drops 9.14x to ~1 ULP (0.000854), BUT the divergence STILL accumulates diffusely (L30~0.12, L58~0.19), STILL explodes at deep full-attn (L59~1.3, L63~33.75, final_norm max_abs 3.125 cos 0.986) and STILL FLIPS the deep-row argmax (recurrent oracle=3425 vs tree=1970). So for THIS captured carrier the flip is NOT erased by the recurrent oracle — the +89% is an L0-input-frame artifact, but the argmax flip is carried by diffuse fp accumulation that is real vs the non-MTP ground truth. The chunk-vs-recurrent reframe legitimately removes an inflated L0 magnitude (deployment-correct) but is NOT guaranteed to collapse our-spine 5 -> native 3; whether the FRONTIER shrinks is an open empirical question the re-score must answer, and the gap may PERSIST (which would mean a real diffuse defect the recurrent oracle does not hide). Independent corroboration that not all flips are frame artifacts: FR13_GOLD_MARGIN_BIND.md L50-64 finds 2 of 4 forks (p2 gap 2.125, p3 gap 5.125) are large-margin tree-COMMITTER serve deviations (tree serves a rank-2 token its own clean greedy clearly rejects; native E5 is greedy-exact) — a 5-logprob swing is a logic/commit-path defect, NOT a chunk-vs-recurrent ULP and would survive any oracle reframe. Reward-hack decisive criterion (feedback_no_reroute_reward_hacking): switching the oracle to recurrent-no-spec-decode is LEGITIMATE-by-construction ONLY IF native is re-scored vs the SAME recurrent oracle and the reframe is adopted whether or not OUR numbers improve; it is a HACK if applied selectively to soften our count. Playbook: class-10 (shared-source != shared-SASS) — chunked vs recurrent are not just codegen variants, they are different ALGORITHMS (block-parallel WY vs sequential rank-1 roll) with different reduction order; "bit-exact by re-execution" is invalid across them; class-12 (measurement traps / frame) — this is exactly a frame trap (oracle kernel != deployment kernel), and the fix is to pin the oracle to the deployment recurrent path, but with the class-12 discipline of re-scoring BOTH arms and not concluding "+2 was frame" until the full-stream re-score (not a single row) shows it. adv.rewardHackVerdict: LEGITIMATE-by-construction ONLY UNDER DISCIPLINE — not a foregone clean correction, and not an unconditional hack. The banned pattern (feedback_no_reroute_reward_hacking) is changing WHAT COMPUTES the deliverable (routing the spine through native's kernel while our kernel stays wrong); that is NOT this case — the deliverable tree-scan kernel is untouched. Here only the REFERENCE oracle changes. The decisive criterion has two parts. PART A (does it measure deployment?): SETTLED by code = YES. Recurrent no-spec DECODE is exactly the kernel vLLM runs without speculation (query_len==1 -> num_decodes>0 -> fused_sigmoid_gating / _forward_core_decode_non_spec single-step roll, gdn_linear_attn.py L1163/L1261-1307); the chunked re-prefill is a stricter-than-reality proxy that adds a ~9x chunk-vs-recurrent ULP frame (q1: 0.0078 chunked vs 0.000854 recurrent at L0). PART B (does native re-scored vs the SAME oracle also collapse, or does the gap persist?): OPEN — must be answered empirically before adopting. It becomes a HACK iff applied to our arm but native is not re-scored vs the identical oracle, OR '+2 was frame' is declared from the single q1 row not a full-stream re-score, OR it is adopted because our number improved. Class-12 discipline (playbook row 12): re-score BOTH arms; class-10 (row 10): chunked vs recurrent are different algorithms (block-parallel WY vs sequential rank-1), so 'bit-exact by re-execution' across them is invalid. Independent guard that it is NOT a blanket softener: the SAME chunked teacher-force (fr13_gold_margin_probe.py L411-424) already caught real large-margin tree-COMMITTER defects (gold-margin p2 gap 2.125, p3 gap 5.125, both backends agree the argmax) — those survive ANY oracle reframe.
adv.gapShrinksOrPersists: MIXED / OPEN — the re-score must answer it; not foregone. Predicted-shrink component (legitimate frame removal): q1 proves the L0 carrier magnitude is ~89% chunk-vs-recurrent; re-scored vs recurrent, our-spine L0 drops to ~1 bf16 ULP (0.000854). Native E5's gap vs chunked is already smaller (its MTP-5 verify is the same kernel family vLLM tunes for prefill/decode), so re-scoring native moves it LESS than it moves ours — direction predicts our-spine 5 -> toward native 3 IF the gap were purely L0-input-frame. BUT persist component (real defect the recurrent oracle does NOT hide): for the q1 deep-row carrier the divergence STILL accumulates diffusely vs the recurrent oracle (L30~0.12, L58~0.19), STILL explodes at deep full-attn (L59~1.3, L63~33.75, final_norm max_abs 3.125, cos 0.986) and STILL FLIPS the deep-row argmax (recurrent oracle=3425 vs tree=1970). And the gold-margin p2/p3 committer defects (5-logprob swings, both backends agree) are logic/commit-path defects, not chunk-vs-recurrent ULPs, and survive any reframe. So the e2e both-arm re-score would show: near-tie-band flips shrink (frame artifact removed legitimately) while diffuse-accumulation deep flips and committer-path defects persist (real loss). Whether the net our-spine count collapses to ~native 3 (frame) or stays at 5 (residual real diffuse defect) is the open empirical question — NOT assumed.
adv.userQuestion: Two coupled decisions. (1) ORACLE FRAME (lineage-affecting, STOPS for your ruling per GDN-kernel-lineage policy): the binding flip oracle fr13_oracle_stream_teacher_force.py measures EVERY flip count (cat9 22 / our-spine 5 / native 3) against a CHUNKED per-position re-prefill — proven by code (Qwen3-Next lacks SupportsMambaPrefixCaching -> forced align block-granular cache -> the prompt+served[:i] partial-block suffix is re-chunked via chunk_gated_delta_rule, not the recurrent roll). This VIOLATES the directive's own anchor 'oracle=no-spec NOT prefill' and inflates the near-tie band by a ~9x chunk-vs-recurrent ULP frame (q1). Should the lossless flip oracle be switched to the recurrent no-spec DECODE — the kernel deployment actually runs without speculation? (2) BUILD THE INSTRUMENT: should I build the in-process recurrent no-spec single-step decode oracle (option b/c — load the model once, decode served_ids one token at a time carrying ssm_state/conv_state forward, read each step's distribution directly so the streamed off-by-one is sidestepped) and re-score BOTH arms + cat9 on the FULL stream, to settle empirically whether the native-vs-ours gap shrinks to ~0 (the +2 was a frame artifact -> reframe is a clean deployment-correct correction) or persists (ours has a real diffuse defect the recurrent oracle would NOT hide)? My recommendation: YES to building the both-arm in-process re-score (decision 2) BEFORE ruling on decision 1, because the q1 deep-row flip and the gold-margin p2/p3 committer defects prove the answer is not foregone, and the reframe is legitimate ONLY if both arms are re-scored and the frame is adopted regardless of whether our number improves.
adv.recommendation: Build the in-process recurrent no-spec single-step DECODE oracle (option b/c: load model once, decode served_ids one-at-a-time carrying ssm_state/conv_state forward, read each step's max_tokens=1 distribution directly — no HTTP re-prefill, no streamed-array indexing so the off-by-one is sidestepped) and re-score BOTH arms (our pure spine AND native E5, AND cat9) against it for the FULL stream, not the single q1 row. This is the only instrument that simultaneously (i) measures what no-spec deployment actually does, (ii) sidesteps the streamed off-by-one, and (iii) re-scores native vs the identical oracle so the Part-B question is answered. Adopt the recurrent frame as the lossless flip oracle iff that both-arm re-score is run and the frame is adopted regardless of whether our count improves. Until that re-score exists, do NOT restate the 5/3/22 frontier as 'frame-corrected' and do NOT retire the +2 — the deep-row flip and gold-margin committer defects show real non-frame loss remains in the mix. (Verify-phase: recommend, do not build; do not modify the instrument or re-baseline.)
adv.issues: Adversarial caveats carried into the package, none overturning holds=True: (1) The reframe must NOT be over-claimed as '+2 was frame' — that conclusion requires the full-stream both-arm re-score; the single q1 row shows the L0 MAGNITUDE is ~89% frame but the deep-row ARGMAX FLIP still persists vs the recurrent oracle, so the frontier is NOT proven to collapse. (2) Recurrent is itself TWO kernels: the tree arm uses the SPEC recurrent kernel (fused_sigmoid_gating, IS_SPEC_DECODING) while no-spec deployment uses the PACKED-DECODE recurrent kernel (fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode) — ~1 ULP apart, both != chunked; the deployment-correct lossless reference is the no-spec packed-decode recurrent, and the tree arm is scored against it within the self-noise floor (the user's existing within-floor bar), not byte-identical. (3) Feasibility blocker: a TRUE recurrent re-score CANNOT be an HTTP /v1/completions loop (every such request re-prefills/re-chunks because Qwen3-Next has no sub-block recurrent-state preservation and no 'resume from saved SSM state' API hook) — it MUST be an in-process model harness. Option (a) single streaming no-spec decode with corrected off-by-one is cheapest but rests on the distrusted streamed-logprob alignment, so (b)/(c) in-process is the robust path. (4) Independent corroboration that the chunked oracle does NOT blanket-hide loss (kills the 'softer reference' worry at the high-margin end): the same chunked teacher-force already caught gold-margin p2/p3 real committer defects (5-logprob swings, both backends agree the argmax) — those are logic/commit-path defects, not ULPs, and survive any reframe.
